questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Kedu ụdaume so n'otu ndakọrịta ụdaume (vowel harmony set) na 'i'?
questions.explanation: In Igbo vowel harmony, vowels group into two sets by tongue root position; 'i' pairs with 'ị' in usage patterns learners must distinguish.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Olee ihe kpatara akara olu (tone marks) ji dị mkpa n'ederede Igbo?
options: N'ihi na olu dị iche iche nwere ike ime ka otu mkpụrụedemede pụta ihe abụọ ma ọ bụ karịa
N'ihi na ha na-eme ka akwụkwọ dị mma ile anya naanị
questions.explanation: Tone is contrastive in Igbo, meaning the same sequence of letters can carry different meanings depending on the tone pattern, which is why tone marks matter.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Kedu okwu Igbo abụọ a na-esi n'olu ha mata ọdịiche n'ihe ha pụtara, ọ bụ ezie na e dere ha otu ụzọ n'edemede na-enweghị akara olu?
questions.explanation: 'Akwụ' is a classic Igbo example of tonal minimal pairs, where identical spelling without tone marks can represent distinct words such as palm nut and bed, depending on tone.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Kedu ụdị mgbochiume (consonant) a na-akpọ 'gb' n'ụtọasụsụ ụdaasụsụ Igbo?
options: Mgbochiume abụọ jikọrọ ọnụ (digraph) na-egosipụta otu ụda
questions.explanation: 'Gb', like 'gh', 'kp', 'nw' and 'ny', is a digraph in the Igbo alphabet — two letters representing a single distinct consonant sound.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Kedu ihe a na-akpọ mgbanwe ụda mkpụrụokwu na-eme mgbe mkpụrụokwu abụọ zutere n'ọnụ n'ekwuwa okwu (elision/assimilation)?
questions.explanation: Assimilation and elision describe how adjoining sounds influence and sometimes merge with each other in fluent Igbo speech.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Olu ole bụ isi ka ọ bara n'usoro olu Igbo, ewezuga olu agbadaba (downstep)?
options: Abụọ: olu elu na olu ala
questions.explanation: Igbo tone is fundamentally binary: high and low, with downstep recognised as a derived variant of high tone rather than a fully separate basic tone.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Kedu ihe a na-akpọ mgbochiume nsi-imi na-eguzo n'ọnọdụ ụdaume n'okwu dịka 'nne'?
questions.explanation: Nasal consonants like 'n' and 'm' can serve as the nucleus of a syllable in Igbo, standing in for a vowel.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: N'asụsụ Igbo, olee otu e si ekwu okwu 'akwa' iji pụta 'cloth' karịa 'egg' ma e dee ya n'enweghị akara olu?
options: Ọ dịghị ụzọ e si ama ọdịiche ha
E ji ọnụọgụ mkpụrụedemede dị iche iche dee ya
E ji olu (tone) dị iche iche kpọọ ya
E ji mgbochiume dị iche iche dee ya
questions.explanation: 'Akwa' is another commonly cited Igbo tonal minimal-pair word: identical spelling but distinct meanings (egg, cloth, cry, bridge) distinguished by tone alone.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Kedu ihe a na-akpọ akụkụ ụdaasụsụ na-elebara anya n'otu e si esite n'ọnụ mmadụ mepụta ụda?
questions.explanation: Phonetics (ụdaasụsụ) is the branch of study focused on how speech sounds are physically produced, transmitted, and perceived.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Kedu nkọwa kacha zie ezi maka mkpụrụedemede mmechi (closed syllable) n'asụsụ Igbo?
options: Mkpụrụedemede na-akwụsị na ụdaume mgbe niile
questions.explanation: A closed syllable ends in a consonant sound, in contrast with the open (CV) syllable pattern that dominates ordinary Igbo words.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Kedu ihe a na-akpọ usoro nyocha ụda okwu iji chọpụta ụda dị iche iche pụrụ iche n'otu asụsụ?
questions.explanation: Phonology is the systematic study of how sounds pattern and function meaningfully within a specific language, distinct from the physical study of sounds (phonetics).

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Kedu ihe kpatara ọtụtụ okwu Igbo nwere naanị otu ma ọ bụ mkpụrụedemede abụọ n'ọtụtụ ọnọdụ?
options: N'ihi na Igbo bụ asụsụ nwere mkpụrụedemede CV dị mfe na-emeghachi onwe ya
N'ihi na ọ bụ asụsụ ọhụrụ
questions.explanation: The prevalence of simple, repeating CV syllable structures is a well-known structural feature contributing to the relatively short average word length in Igbo.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Kedu usoro mkpụrụedemede a na-eji ede Igbo izugbe taa?
questions.explanation: The Onwu orthography, adopted officially in 1961, remains the standard writing system used for modern standard Igbo.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Kedu ihe a na-akpọ okwu abụọ e jikọtara ọnụ iji mepụta otu okwu ọhụrụ nwere ihe ọ pụtara, dịka 'ụlọ' na 'akwụkwọ' bụ 'ụlọakwụkwọ'?
questions.explanation: 'Ụlọakwụkwọ' (school) exemplifies Igbo compounding, where two independent words combine to form a new word with a distinct meaning.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Kedu ihe a na-akpọ mkpụrụokwu ndị dịka 'sukuu', 'motọ', na 'kọmputa' e webatara n'asụsụ Igbo?
questions.explanation: Words like 'sukuu' (school), 'motọ' (motor) and 'kọmputa' (computer) are loan words absorbed into Igbo, mostly from English, and adapted to Igbo sound patterns.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Kedu mgbakwunye a na-etinye n'ihu mkpụrụokwu iji gbanwee ma ọ bụ kwado ihe ọ pụtara (prefix)?
questions.explanation: A prefix (mgbakwunye ihu) is attached to the beginning of a root word, one of the two main affix positions in Igbo morphology alongside the suffix.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Site n'okwu mgbagwoju 'ọzụzụ', kedu mkpụrụokwu (root) a na-esi eleta ya?
questions.explanation: The verb root '-zụ-' (to train/rear) underlies derived and reduplicated forms such as 'ọzụzụ' (training/rearing) in Igbo morphology.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Kedu ihe a na-akpọ okwu ọdịnaala dị iche na mpaghara Igbo dị iche iche na-akọwa otu ihe, dịka 'ji' na mpaghara ụfọdụ, ebe mpaghara ọzọ nwere aha ọzọ?
questions.explanation: Igbo has many regional dialects, and dialect words reflect the natural variation in vocabulary used across different Igbo-speaking areas for the same concept.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Olee ihe a na-eji akọwa 'mkpụrụokwu' n'ụzọ dị mfe n'asụsụ Igbo?
options: Otu mgbọrọgwụ okwu ma ọ bụ ngwakọta okwu nwere ihe ọ pụtara
questions.explanation: A word (mkpụrụokwu) is a basic meaningful unit of language, whether a single root or a combination of morphemes.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Kedu isi ihe kpatara e ji ahazi okwu Igbo n'akwụkwọ ọkọwa okwu (dictionary) n'usoro mkpụrụedemede?
options: Ka okwu niile dịrị otu ogologo
Ka o mee ka ịchọta okwu dị mfe na ngwa ngwa
Ka a hapụ akara olu niile
questions.explanation: Alphabetical ordering in dictionaries makes it fast and predictable for users to locate any given word.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Kedu ihe a na-akpọ okwu Igbo na-egosi otu ihe ma ọ bụ omume n'ụzọ dị nro, karịa nkọwa ozugbo (idiomatic expression)?
questions.explanation: An idiom (akpaokwu) is a fixed expression whose figurative meaning differs from a literal, word-for-word reading, distinct from a proverb which usually carries a moral lesson.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Kedu mkpụrụokwu a ga-eji dochie 'nnukwu' n'ahịrịokwu, ma ihe ọ pụtara ghara ịgbanwe nke ukwuu?
questions.explanation: 'Ukwu' (as in 'ukwu ukwu' / large) functions as a near-synonym of 'nnukwu' (big/great) in describing size.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Kedu ọdịiche dị n'etiti 'ilu' na 'akpaokwu' n'asụsụ Igbo?
options: Ilu na-ebukarị ozizi omume ma ọ bụ amamihe, ebe akpaokwu bụ naanị nkebiokwu nwere ihe ọ pụtara na-abụghị nke ozugbo
questions.explanation: Proverbs (ilu) typically encode a moral lesson or wisdom, while idioms (akpaokwu) are fixed figurative phrases without necessarily carrying moral instruction.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Kedu ihe a na-akpọ akwụkwọ e ji achọpụta ihe okwu Igbo pụtara na Bekee ma ọ bụ asụsụ ọzọ?
questions.explanation: A dictionary (akwụkwọ ọkọwa okwu) provides the meanings, and often translations, of words in a language.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Kedu klaasị okwu (mkpọaha) so n'ime ndị a: 'nwoke', 'ụlọ', 'echiche'?
questions.explanation: 'Nwoke' (man), 'ụlọ' (house) and 'echiche' (thought/idea) are all nouns, naming a person, a place/thing, and an abstract idea respectively.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: N'ahịrịokwu 'Nwata ahụ na-agba ọsọ', kedu okwu bụ ngwaa (verb)?
questions.explanation: 'Na-agba' (is running) is the verb phrase expressing the ongoing action performed by the subject 'nwata ahụ'.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Kedu klaasị okwu 'ọma' bụ n'ahịrịokwu 'nwanyị ọma ahụ bịara'?
questions.explanation: 'Ọma' (good) describes the noun 'nwanyị' (woman), functioning as an adjective.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Kedu ihe a na-akpọ okwu na-anọchi anya mkpọaha iji zere ịkwụghachi aha ahụ ugboro ugboro?
questions.explanation: A pronoun (nnochi aha), like 'ọ', 'ha', or 'anyị', substitutes for a noun to avoid repetition.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: N'ahịrịokwu 'O bikere n'elu oche', kedu klaasị okwu 'n'elu' bụ?
questions.explanation: 'N'elu' (on top of) shows the spatial relationship between the subject and 'oche' (chair), making it a preposition.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Kedu njikọ okwu a ga-eji jikọta ahịrịokwu abụọ ndị a: 'Ọ dara ụra ___ a kpọrọ ya oku'?
questions.explanation: 'Mana' (but) correctly links the contrasting clauses of falling asleep and being called, expressing contrast.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Kedu ihe a na-akpọ ahịrịokwu na-ajụ ajụjụ, dịka 'Kedu ebe ị na-aga?'
questions.explanation: An interrogative sentence is used to ask a question, marked in Igbo by question words such as 'kedu' or a rising tone pattern.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Kedu ụdị ahịrịokwu bụ 'Mechie ụzọ ahụ!'?
questions.explanation: 'Mechie ụzọ ahụ!' (Close the door!) issues a direct command, characteristic of an imperative sentence.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: N'ụtọasụsụ Igbo, kedu ọnọdụ mkpọaha na-anọ n'ahịrịokwu dị mfe dịka 'Chidi ___ akpụkpọụkwụ'?
options: Ihe a na-arụ ọrụ na ya (object)
questions.explanation: 'Chidi' functions as the subject (onye ọrụ), the one performing the action, at the start of a typical Igbo SVO sentence.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Kedu ihe a na-akpọ mgbanwe ngwaa iji gosipụta na omume ahụ emeela n'oge gara aga (past tense)?
options: Mgbanwe oge gara aga (past tense marking)
questions.explanation: Igbo verbs take tense/aspect markers to indicate when an action occurred, including markers used for completed past actions.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Kedu ihe a na-akpọ nkebi ụtọasụsụ na-elebara anya n'usoro mkpụrụokwu si emepụta ọzọ (word formation)?
questions.explanation: Morphology studies how words are formed and structured from smaller meaningful units such as roots and affixes.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Kedu ihe a na-akpọ ahịrịokwu na-adaberekarị n'ahịrịokwu ọzọ iji zuo ezu (complex sentence)?
questions.explanation: A complex sentence contains a main clause and at least one dependent clause that relies on the main clause for full meaning.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: N'ahịrịokwu 'Ha na-eri nri', kedu okwu bụ ihe a na-arụ ọrụ na ya (object)?
questions.explanation: 'Nri' (food) receives the action of eating, making it the object of the verb 'na-eri' (are eating).

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Kedu ihe a na-akpọ mgbakwunye e tinyere n'azụ mkpụrụokwu iji gbanwee ọnọdụ ya (suffix)?
questions.explanation: A suffix (mgbakwunye azụ) attaches to the end of a root word, one of the two principal affix positions in Igbo.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: N'ịgụta edemede iji ghọta ya (comprehension), gịnị bụ isi ihe a na-achọ n'aka onye na-agụ ya?
options: Ịghọta isi ozi na nkọwa dị n'edemede ma zaa ajụjụ ndị metụtara ya
Ịmata naanị aha onye dere ya
questions.explanation: The primary goal of comprehension practice is to understand a passage's content and details well enough to answer related questions accurately.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Kedu ụdị edemede na-akọ ihe mere eme n'usoro (narrative essay)?
questions.explanation: A narrative essay recounts events in a sequence, typically with a beginning, middle, and end.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Kedu ụdị edemede a na-eji akọwapụta onye, ebe, ma ọ bụ ihe n'ụzọ zuru ezu iji mee ka onye na-agụ ya hụ ya n'anya uche?
questions.explanation: A descriptive essay uses vivid detail to help the reader form a clear mental picture of a person, place, or thing.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: N'ide akwụkwọ ozi obere (informal letter) n'asụsụ Igbo, gịnị ka a na-ejikarị amalite ya?
options: Ekele na aha onye e degaara akwụkwọ ozi ahụ
questions.explanation: Igbo letters conventionally open with a greeting and an address to the recipient before moving to the main message.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Kedu nkà kacha mkpa maka ide edemede zuru oke n'asụsụ Igbo?
options: Ide n'enweghị akara olu ọ bụla
Nhazi echiche n'usoro doro anya na iji ụtọasụsụ ziri ezi
questions.explanation: Good essay writing requires clear, logical organisation of ideas along with correct grammar.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Mgbe a na-agụ otu edemede ọgụgụ isi, gịnị bụ ụzọ kacha mma iji chọpụta azịza ajụjụ ma ị na-echedoghị echiche?
options: Ịzaghachi site na ntụle aha onwe gị
Ịlaghachi azụ gụọ akụkụ metụtara ajụjụ ahụ ọzọ
Ịchọpụta azịza site n'echiche onwe gị naanị
questions.explanation: Re-reading the relevant section of the passage before answering is the most reliable way to confirm the correct answer.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Kedu ihe a na-akpọ nkọwa nkenke nke isi ihe dị n'otu edemede ogologo?
questions.explanation: A summary (nchịkọta) briefly captures the essential main points of a longer text without every minor detail.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Kedu ụdị edemede na-egosipụta echiche onye na-ede ya ma jiri ihe akaebe kwado ya (argumentative essay)?
questions.explanation: An argumentative essay presents and supports a clear position on an issue using logical reasoning and evidence.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: N'ide akwụkwọ ozi gọọmentị/azụmahịa (formal letter) n'Igbo, gịnị dị iche na akwụkwọ ozi obere?
options: Ọ na-achọkarị okwu na usoro nkwanye ùgwù karịa
Ọ dịghị mkpa ekele ọ bụla
Ọ na-adịkarị mkpụmkpụ karịa akwụkwọ ozi obere
Ọ naghị enwe onye a na-edegara ya
questions.explanation: Formal letters typically demand more careful, respectful, and structured language compared to informal letters to friends or family.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Kedu ihe kpatara a na-agba mbọ ịmụta ụtọasụsụ ziri ezi tupu e wee mụọ ide edemede n'asụsụ Igbo?
options: N'ihi na ọ dịghị mkpa n'ọmụmụ asụsụ
N'ihi na akara olu adịghị emetụta ụtọasụsụ
N'ihi na ụtọasụsụ ziri ezi na-eme ka echiche pụta ìhè nke ọma n'edemede
N'ihi na ụtọasụsụ bụ naanị maka mgbako
questions.explanation: A solid grasp of grammar helps writers express ideas clearly and correctly in their essays.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Kedu nkọwa kacha zie ezi maka Agụmagụ Ọnụ n'omenala Igbo?
options: Agụmagụ e siri na mba ọzọ tụgharịa
Agụmagụ e si n'ọnụ na-agbasa site n'ọgbọ ruo n'ọgbọ, n'edeghị ede ya
questions.explanation: Oral literature (Agụmagụ Ọnụ) is transmitted verbally across generations rather than through writing.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Kedu ihe a na-akpọ akụkọ ọdịnala na-akọwa mmalite ụwa ma ọ bụ ihe omimi banyere chi na mmụọ?
questions.explanation: Myths (nkọmịrịkọ) explain the origins of the world or supernatural phenomena in Igbo oral tradition.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Kedu ihe a na-akpọ akụkọ ọdịnala metụtara ndị dị ike ma ọ bụ ihe omume mere n'oge gara aga, nke ndị mmadụ na-ekwenyekarị na e nwere eziokwu dị na ya?
questions.explanation: Legends (nkọkịrịkọ) recount notable figures or events believed to hold a kernel of historical truth.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Kedu ihe a na-akpọ akụkọ ifo na-abụkarị maka anụmanụ dị iche iche na-ekwu okwu dịka mmadụ (dịka Mbekwu na Odum)?
questions.explanation: Igbo folktales (akụkọ ifo) frequently feature anthropomorphised animal characters such as the tortoise (Mbekwu/Mbe) and lion (Odum), teaching moral lessons through their adventures.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: N'akụkọ ifo Igbo, kedu anụmanụ a maara nke ọma dịka onye aghụghọ na onye amamihe (trickster) n'akụkọ ọtụtụ?
questions.explanation: The tortoise (mbekwu/mbe) is the archetypal trickster figure in Igbo folktales, known for cunning and cleverness that often gets it into and out of trouble.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Kedu ihe a na-akpọ ajụjụ nwere ọkịkọ nke a na-eji egwuri egwu iji nwalee amamihe na uche ọsọ ọsọ?
questions.explanation: Riddles (agwụgwa) are a traditional guessing game designed to test cleverness and quick thinking.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Kedu ihe a na-akpọ abụ ọdịnala nke a na-abụkarị n'oge mmemme, ọrụ ubi, ma ọ bụ n'egwuregwu ụmụaka?
questions.explanation: Traditional songs (egwu ọdịnala) accompany festivals, communal work, and children's play in Igbo culture.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Kedu ihe a na-akpọ okwu amamihe dị mkpụmkpụ ndị okenye na-ejikarị akụziri ụmụ ntị (ilu)?
questions.explanation: Proverbs (ilu) are short, wise sayings elders use to teach and pass on values and wisdom.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: N'ilu Igbo a ma ama, 'Ọ bụrụ na anyanwụ apụọ, ọ ga-acha nkịta ọcha ọcha' na-akọwapụta gịnị?
options: Eziokwu ga-apụta ìhè n'agbanyeghị mgbe ọ ga-adị
Ọ dịghị isi ihe ọ pụtara
questions.explanation: This proverb-style saying is a common way Igbo proverbs use natural imagery to teach that truth or reality eventually becomes clear, regardless of delay.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Kedu isi ọrụ ilu (proverbs) na-arụ n'ikwu okwu n'ọdịnala Igbo?
options: Ọ na-eme ka okwu doo anya, mee ka ọ dị ike, wee gosipụta amamihe onye na-ekwu okwu
Ọ bụ naanị maka ntụrụndụ ụmụaka
questions.explanation: Proverbs enrich speech, add persuasive weight, and demonstrate the speaker's wisdom and command of the culture.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Kedu oge a na-akpọkarị agwụgwa (riddles) n'omenala Igbo ochie?
options: Naanị n'oge ememme ọlụlụ di na nwunye
questions.explanation: Riddle-telling sessions traditionally happened at night, providing entertainment and mental exercise after the day's work.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Kedu ọrụ ndị okenye (elders) na-arụkarị n'ịgbasa agụmagụ ọnụ n'obodo Igbo?
options: Ha na-akọrọ ụmụaka na ndị na-eto eto akụkọ ifo, ilu, na amamihe ọdịnala
Ha na-akọwakarị naanị akụkọ mba ofesi
Ha anaghị etinye aka n'agụmagụ ọnụ ma ọ bụla
questions.explanation: Elders serve as the traditional custodians and transmitters of oral literature, passing folktales, proverbs, and wisdom to younger generations.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Kedu ụdị egwu ọdịnala Igbo a na-eji anabata ndị ọbịa ma ọ bụ mee ememme dị iche iche, jiri ọdụdụ egwu na ihe egwu ọdịnala?
options: Egwu na Ọdụdụ Ọdịnala (traditional music and dance)
questions.explanation: Traditional music and dance are central to welcoming guests and celebrating festivals in Igbo communities.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Gịnị bụ isi ọdịiche dị n'etiti nkọmịrịkọ (myth) na nkọkịrịkọ (legend)?
options: Nkọkịrịkọ bụ naanị maka egwu ntụrụndụ
Nkọmịrịkọ na-emetụta ihe omimi na chi, ebe nkọkịrịkọ na-emetụtakarị ndị mmadụ ma ọ bụ ihe omume dị n'akụkọ ihe mere eme
questions.explanation: Myths deal with supernatural or divine explanations, while legends focus more on human figures or events with a claimed historical basis.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Kedu ihe ga-eme ma ọ bụrụ na a ghara ịchekwa agụmagụ ọnụ site n'ọgbọ ruo n'ọgbọ?
options: A ga-enwe agụmagụ ọnụ karịa mbụ
A ga-efu ọtụtụ ọdịnala na amamihe ndị dị mkpa nke ọdịnala ahụ
Ọdịnala ahụ ga-adịgide na-enweghị mgbanwe ọ bụla
Ọ dịghị ihe ga-emeru omenala ahụ
questions.explanation: Without deliberate transmission across generations, much valuable oral tradition and cultural wisdom risks being permanently lost.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Kedu ihe a na-akpọ mkpịsị akụkọ ifo na-emesịkarị egosi omume ọjọọ ka a taa ya ahụhụ, ebe omume ọma ka a kwụghachi ụgwọ ọma?
questions.explanation: Igbo folktales typically end with a clear moral lesson, rewarding good behaviour and punishing bad conduct.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Kedu ụdị nkà a na-achọkarị n'aka onye na-akọ akụkọ ifo n'ihu ọha (oral performer) ka akụkọ ya na-atọ ndị na-ege ntị ụtọ?
options: Ikike iji olu na omume ahụ mee ka akụkọ ahụ dị mma ma dọrọ mmasị
Ikike ịkpọ egwu ọ bụla na-enweghị olu
questions.explanation: Skilled oral performers use vocal expression, gesture, and audience interaction (often call-and-response) to make storytelling engaging.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Kedu ọrụ egwu ubi (farm/work songs) na-arụ n'omenala Igbo?
options: Ọ na-akwalite ume ndị ọrụ ma na-eme ka ọrụ ọha dịrị mma
Ọ metụtara mgbanwe ihu igwe naanị
questions.explanation: Farm work songs energise labourers and help coordinate communal effort, making shared work more efficient and enjoyable.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Kedu ihe a na-akpọ nkatakọtọ (chorus/refrain) a na-eji na-azaghachi n'egwu ọdịnala ma ọ bụ n'akụkọ ifo?
questions.explanation: Call-and-response is a defining performance feature of Igbo oral tradition, where a leader's line is answered by a group's refrain.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Kedu ihe kpatara e ji akpọ agwụgwa (riddles) 'egwuregwu okwu' n'asụsụ Bekee?
options: N'ihi na ọ bụ egwuregwu na-eji okwu chọpụta amamihe onye na-aza ya
N'ihi na e ji ya achọ ego
N'ihi na a naghị eji ya eme ihe ọ bụla
N'ihi na ọ bụ naanị maka ndị ọka
questions.explanation: Riddles are essentially a verbal 'word game' testing cleverness through language rather than physical skill.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Kedu ihe a na-akpọ agụmagụ e dere n'akwụkwọ, dị ka akụkọ, egwuregwu, na abụ e dere ede?
questions.explanation: Written literature (Agụmagụ Edere Ede) refers to literary works recorded in text form, distinct from orally transmitted traditions.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Kedu onye e ji ama dịka otu n'ime ndị mbụ dere akwụkwọ akụkọ Igbo a maara nke ọma, dịka 'Omenụkọ'?
questions.explanation: Pita Nwana is widely credited as the author of 'Omenụkọ', one of the earliest and most influential Igbo-language novels.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Kedu ụdị agụmagụ edere ede a na-akpọ nke a na-eme dịka egwuregwu ihu ọha, nwere ndị ọrụnnọgbu na-ekwu okwu (drama)?
questions.explanation: Drama (egwuregwu) is a literary genre written to be performed, featuring characters speaking dialogue, distinct from prose and poetry.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: N'agụmagụ edere ede, kedu ihe a na-akpọ isi ozi ma ọ bụ echiche bụ isi nke onye edemede na-achọ ịkọwa n'ime akwụkwọ ya?
questions.explanation: The theme (isi ihe) is the central underlying message or idea an author conveys through a literary work.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Kedu ihe a na-akpọ ndị mmadụ dị iche iche na-eme ihe n'ime otu akụkọ ma ọ bụ egwuregwu?
questions.explanation: Characters are the individuals who participate in and drive the events of a narrative or dramatic work.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Kedu ihe a na-akpọ akụkọ e dere ede n'akwụkwọ ogologo nwere isi ihe na ndị ọrụnnọgbu zuru oke (novel)?
questions.explanation: A novel (akụkọ ogologo) is an extended fictional prose narrative with developed characters and plot.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Kedu ọrụ JAMB/Ule ule si etinye n'usoro mmụta banyere agụmagụ edere ede Igbo?
options: Ọ na-elebara anya naanị na akụkọ mba ọzọ
Ọ naghị enwe ihe ọ bụla metụtara agụmagụ edere ede
Ọ na-ahọpụta akwụkwọ akụkọ, egwuregwu, na abụ ụfọdụ ka ụmụ akwụkwọ mụọ maka ule
questions.explanation: Examination bodies prescribe specific Igbo prose, drama, and poetry texts that candidates are expected to study.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Kedu nkà dị mkpa maka nyocha (analysis) nke otu akụkọ ma ọ bụ egwuregwu e dere ede n'asụsụ Igbo?
options: Ikike ịgụ akwụkwọ ngwa ngwa n'enweghị nghọta
Ikike ịchọpụta isi ihe, ndị ọrụnnọgbu, na ọnọdụ akụkọ ahụ
questions.explanation: Effective literary analysis requires identifying a text's theme, characters, and setting for deeper understanding.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Gịnị bụ isi ọdịiche dị n'etiti agụmagụ ọnụ na agụmagụ edere ede?
options: Agụmagụ ọnụ ka a na-agbasa site n'ọnụ, ebe agụmagụ edere ede ka a na-edekọ n'akwụkwọ
Ọ dịghị ọdịiche dị n'etiti ha
Agụmagụ edere ede bụ naanị maka mmemme ọlụlụ di na nwunye
questions.explanation: The core distinction lies in mode of preservation: oral literature is passed down verbally while written literature is recorded in text.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Kedu ụdị agụmagụ edere ede a na-eji ahịrịokwu dị nro na akara ụda mee ka echiche pụta ìhè n'ụzọ dị mma (poetry)?
questions.explanation: Poetry (uri) uses carefully crafted, often rhythmic language to express ideas and emotions in a compact, artistic form.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Kedu ihe a na-akpọ usoro alụmdi na nwunye n'ọdịnala Igbo, nke gụnyere ịkwụ ụgwọ ọlụlụ?
options: Alụmdi na nwunye ọdịnala (traditional marriage institution)
questions.explanation: Traditional Igbo marriage (alụmdi na nwunye) involves formal family negotiations, including the payment of bride price (ịkwụ ụgwọ ọlụlụ).

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Kedu ihe a na-akpọ mmemme e ji enye nwa ọhụrụ aha ya n'ọdịnala Igbo?
questions.explanation: The naming ceremony (ịgụ aha) formally gives a newborn their name, usually accompanied by prayers and celebration.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Kedu ihe a na-akpọ ọchịchị ọdịnala Igbo nke a na-ahọpụta ndị okenye ma ọ bụ eze n'obodo iji chịa obodo dịka omenala si dị?
options: Ọchịchị Ala/Ọha na Eze (traditional council/monarchy system)
questions.explanation: Many Igbo communities are traditionally governed by a council of elders (Ọha na Eze) or a traditional ruler, depending on local custom.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Kedu ihe a na-akpọ akwa mgba nwoke ma ọ bụ nwaanyị na-eyi n'oge emume ọdịnala dị mkpa dịka mmanwụ?
questions.explanation: Traditional attire (akwa omenala) is worn during significant cultural events such as masquerade festivals and title-taking ceremonies.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Kedu ihe a na-akpọ mmemme nzuzo dị mkpa n'omenala Igbo ebe mmadụ na-eyiri uwe ma na-anọchite anya mmụọ ndị nna nna ha (dịka na ememme Ahịajiọkụ ma ọ bụ ememme mkpọmasị)?
questions.explanation: The masquerade (mmụọ/mmanwụ) tradition, in which performers embody ancestral or spiritual figures, is a central feature of many Igbo festivals.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Kedu ihe a na-akpọ ememme owuwe ihe ubi a na-eme kwa afọ n'ọtụtụ obodo Igbo iji kelee ihe ubi ọhụrụ, dịka ji?
questions.explanation: The New Yam Festival (Iri Ji/Iwa Ji) is an annual harvest celebration held across many Igbo communities to mark the yam harvest with thanksgiving.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Kedu ihe a na-akpọ nsọpụrụ ndị Igbo na-enye chi ha, mmụọ ha, na ndị nna nna ha nwụrụ anwụ n'omenala ochie?
options: Nsọpụrụ ndịichie na chi (ancestral and spiritual reverence)
Ọ dịghị nsọpụrụ ọ bụla dị
questions.explanation: Traditional Igbo religion and culture place great importance on honouring ancestors (ndịichie) and spiritual/deity figures (chi/arụsị).

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Kedu ihe a na-akpọ omenala mbụ e ji anabata onye ọbịa n'ụlọ Igbo, dịka ịnye ya mmiri ma ọ bụ ọjị?
questions.explanation: Igbo hospitality customs, such as offering water or kola nut (ọjị) to guests, reflect deeply held cultural values of welcome and respect.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Kedu ihe a na-akpọ ọji (kola nut) na-anọchi anya ya n'omenala Igbo mgbe a na-agọ ya n'ihu ọbịa?
options: Ọ dịghị isi ihe ọ na-anọchi anya ya
questions.explanation: The breaking and sharing of kola nut (ọjị) symbolises welcome, peace, and mutual respect in Igbo tradition, and is often accompanied by prayers.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Kedu ihe a na-akpọ usoro ọzọ (title-taking) n'omenala Igbo?
options: Usoro e si enweta ọkwa ùgwù n'obodo site n'ịgba mbọ na ịrụ ọrụ maka ọha
questions.explanation: Title-taking (ịgba ọzọ or similar systems) is a traditional process by which a person earns social status and honour within the community.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Kedu ihe a na-akpọ ihe onwunwe ala e ji egosi na ala bụ ihe kacha dị mkpa n'omenala Igbo, karịsịa n'ọrụ ubi?
options: Anyanwụ bụ naanị chi a na-akpọku
Ala bụ chi/nne ala (Earth deity/land reverence)
Ọ dịghị nsọpụrụ e nyere ala
questions.explanation: Ala (the Earth deity) holds a central place in traditional Igbo cosmology, especially given the community's strong dependence on farming and land.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Kedu ihe a na-akpọ ọmarịcha ihe owuwu ụlọ ọdịnala Igbo bụ isi ebe emume obodo na-ebe (dịka mmemme mmadụ ọha)?
questions.explanation: The village square (ilo/ama) traditionally serves as the community's central gathering place for festivals, meetings, and important events.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Kedu ihe a na-akpọ omenala ịkwa ozu na Igbo, nke gụnyere ememme e ji akwanyere onye nwụrụ anwụ ùgwù?
questions.explanation: Burial and funeral rites (ikwa ozu) are elaborate traditional ceremonies performed to honour the deceased and mark their transition to ancestorhood.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Kedu isi mkpa mmadụ ji akpọ aha ụmụ ya n'ọdịnala Igbo dịka 'Chukwuemeka' ma ọ bụ 'Ngozi'?
options: Aha ndị a na-ahọpụta na-enweghị ihe ọ pụtara
Aha niile na-egosi ọrụ mmadụ na-arụ
Aha ndị a na-egosipụtakarị ekele, ekpere, ma ọ bụ echiche banyere Chineke ma ọ bụ ihe gbasara ọmụmụ nwa
Aha niile a na-esi n'asụsụ Bekee
questions.explanation: Igbo personal names are often meaningful, frequently expressing gratitude, prayer, or circumstances surrounding a child's birth, as with 'Chukwuemeka' (God has done well) or 'Ngozi' (blessing).

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Kedu nzukọ na-elekọta ọganihu na mgbasa asụsụ Igbo n'ọzụzụ akwụkwọ na mgbasa ozi n'oge a?
options: Society for Promoting Igbo Language and Culture (SPILC)
questions.explanation: SPILC is a recognised body actively working to promote and preserve the Igbo language and culture in contemporary Nigeria.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Kedu ihe UNESCO kwuru maka ọdịdị asụsụ Igbo n'ọtụtụ nyocha e mere na mmalite narị afọ 21?
options: Ọ kwuru na Igbo bụ asụsụ ọhụrụ na Naịjirịa
Ọ kwuru na Igbo bụ asụsụ kachasị ọtụtụ ndị na-asụ ya n'ụwa
E nwere nchegbu banyere mbelata ọmụmụ ya n'ụlọ, na-eme ka ndị nkụzi na ndị mmụta chọọ ịgbasi ya mbọ
Ọ kwuru na Igbo enweghị nsogbu ọ bụla
questions.explanation: Concerns about declining intergenerational transmission of Igbo at home have prompted renewed advocacy for its promotion in schools and media.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Kedu teknụzụ ndị a na-eji taa nyere aka gbasaa mmụta na iji asụsụ Igbo, dịka ngwa mkpanaka na weebụsaịtị?
options: Ngwa mọbaịl na weebụsaịtị mmụta asụsụ Igbo
questions.explanation: Mobile apps and websites are increasingly used to teach and promote the Igbo language among younger and diaspora learners.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Kedu ụdị mgbasa ozi (media) na-enyekarị aka ịgbasa asụsụ Igbo n'ụlọ ọrụ redio na telivishọn n'oge a?
options: Mmemme redio na telivishọn e ji Igbo mee (Igbo-language broadcasts)
Ọ dịghị mgbasa ozi Igbo dị
questions.explanation: A number of Nigerian radio and television stations continue to run dedicated Igbo-language programming, helping sustain everyday use of the language.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Kedu isi nsogbu ndị ọka mmụta asụsụ na-ekwukarị maka mbelata iji asụsụ Igbo n'ebe ụmụaka nọ na obodo ukwu?
options: Ọtụtụ nne na nna na-ejikarị Bekee na ụmụ ha na-ekwurịta okwu n'ụlọ
Ọ dịghị nsogbu ọ bụla dị
Ọ dịghị asụsụ Bekee dị na Naịjirịa
questions.explanation: Linguists commonly cite the growing preference for English in urban home communication as a key driver behind declining Igbo fluency among children.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Kedu ihe ndị ọrụ akwụkwọ na-eme iji kwalite mmụta asụsụ Igbo n'ime ụlọ akwụkwọ Naịjirịa n'oge a?
options: Itinye asụsụ Igbo dịka otu asụsụ a na-akụziri ụmụ akwụkwọ na ndị ọzọ dịka ndị so na jamb elective
Iji naanị Bekee kụziere ihe niile
questions.explanation: Igbo continues to be taught as a subject in Nigerian schools and is offered as an elective subject in examinations such as JAMB and Post-UTME screenings.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Kedu ọrụ ndị na-ede n'ederede dijitalụ (dịka Facebook na WhatsApp) na-arụ n'ịgbasa asụsụ Igbo n'oge a?
options: Ha na-enyere aka ka ndị na-asụ Igbo dee ma kparịtaa ụka n'asụsụ ahụ n'ịntanetị
Ha adịghị enye ohere ọ bụla iji Igbo
Ha bụ naanị maka ndị na-asụ Bekee
questions.explanation: Social media platforms have become an important informal space for writing and using Igbo in everyday digital communication.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Kedu ihe a na-akpọ mmemme ememme ọdịnala Igbo a na-eme kwa afọ, nke na-adọtakarị ndị njem si mba ofesi bịa hụ omenala Igbo?
options: Ọ dịghị ememme ọdịnala Igbo dị
Ememme Iri Ji na ememme ọdịnala ndị ọzọ (annual cultural festivals)
questions.explanation: Annual cultural festivals such as the New Yam Festival remain prominent, drawing both local participants and visitors interested in Igbo heritage.
